title: Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for VPN (For Legacy Apps)

blocks.text: With VPN (for Legacy Apps), Private Access (ZPA) can natively support a secondary Layer 3 network-based VPN tunnel for applications and services (e.g., VoIP or server-to-client) that require Layer 3 IP-based connectivity consistent with its Zero Trust security architecture and inside-out connection. From a single client for users and a single console for IT administrators, you can migrate to Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) with Private Access and completely eliminate legacy VPNs. You can accelerate application modernization while retaining access for users during the transition.
This guide takes you through the configuration steps for using VPN (for Legacy Apps) for your organization.
Before the feature can be enabled, make sure that you have:

blocks.item: A private IP address range for the VPN client's IP address pool. The IP address range must not overlap with existing subnets.
A route from the servers to the VPN Service Edge's client IP address pools using a Network Connector's IP address as the next hop.
Ensure that the Network Connector has a route to reach Network segments (the server) that need to be accessed via VPN.

An outbound firewall rule for each Network Connector to the internet. If traffic from the Network Connector to the internet needs to be restricted, an outbound connection to the VPN Service Edge's IP address on the UDP port range from 51820 to 53000 must be allowed, not blocked. This is required to establish a VPN tunnel between the Network Connector and VPN Service Edge. To learn more, see Zscaler Private Access Firewall Allowlist for ZPA ONE or Zscaler Private Access Firewall Allowlist for ZPA TWO. To learn more, see Understanding Zscaler Cloud Names.

blocks.text: VPN (for Legacy Apps) is available to users running supported Zscaler Client Connector versions.

blocks.item: Step 1: Configuring User Enablement

VPN user enablement lets you create VPN rules to manage access to the tunnels. To configure a user enablement rule, you must first define the users. For this step, define the SAML or SCIM attributes for users of VPN (for Legacy Apps). You can also add a posture profile validation in user enablement.
To configure user enablement, see the following articles:
About VPN User Enablement
Configuring VPN User Enablement
See image.
Step 2: (Optional) Adding an External Router

External routers are used for configuring Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) for redundancy to ensure high availability and fault tolerance by providing alternate paths to reach applications during Network Connector node failures and Network Connector to VPN Service Edge path or link failures. This is optional if you have a BGP router.
To configure external routers, see the following articles:
About External Routers
Configuring External Routers
To learn more about configuring redundancy via BGP, see VPN Redundancy Deployment Guide.
Step 3: Configuring a VPN Service Edge
VPN Service Edges manage the connections between Zscaler Client Connector and Network Connectors. Create a VPN Service Edge to specify a service region and provision the client IP pool.
You can use one VPN Service Edge for a tenant, with a default of three VPN Service Edges. Each VPN Service Edge requires a different client IP pool.
To create VPN Service Edges and review recommendations, see the following articles:
About VPN Service Edges
Configuring VPN Service Edges
Step 4: Adding a Network Connector
Network Connectors build a secure VPN tunnel that connects applications to VPN Service Edges. You can configure a single Network Connector per Network Connector group.

To enroll a Network Connector, the recommended method is to use an OAuth 2.0 enrollment token retrieved from the Network Connector's console. To learn more, see the deployment guides for supported platforms.
To create Network Connectors using an OAuth enrollment, see the following articles:
About Network Connectors
Configuring Network Connectors
To create Network Connectors using a provisioning key, see About Network Connector Provisioning Keys.
Step 5: Deploying the Network Connector
To deploy Network Connectors, see the following articles:
Network Connector Software by Platform
Network Connector Deployment Prerequisites
Network Connector Deployment Guide for Linux
Step 6: Verifying the Network Connector Is Added

After deploying the Network Connector and restarting the service, go to the Network Connectors page to verify that the Network Connector appears in the table. To learn more, see About Network Connectors.
Step 7: Adding Network Segments
A Network segment is a local area network (LAN) IP subnet that is assigned to a Network Connector group to define access to servers that are accessed via the VPN tunnel.
To add a Network segment, see the following articles:
About Network Segments
Configuring Network Segments
Step 8: Adding Access Policies
To add access polices, see the following articles:
About VPN Access Policy
Configuring VPN Access Policies
Step 9: Configuring the Client Connector App Profile Bypass VPN Service Edge
Copy the IP address for a VPN Service Edge from the VPN Service Edges page and paste it in the Hostname or IP Address Bypass for VPN Gateway field.
To configure the Client Connector App Profile Bypass, see the following articles:
About VPN Service Edges
Configuring Zscaler Client Connector App Profiles
Step 10: Verifying Connected Users
Verify that users can successfully connect to the VPN Service Edge. To learn more, see About VPN Connected Users.
